newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond spreads hold amid issuance.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond spreads hold amid issuance.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bond spreads were stood firm in the face of brisk new issuance at midday as prices rallied with Treasuries, dealers said.
High-yielders were flat to higher across the spectrum, meanwhile, but traders there said accounts were looking to sell into any strength.

More than $1.0 billion in high-grade debt hit the market by midday, led by Tyco International's $300 million Baa2/BBB-plus rated five-year notes, priced as 6-1/2s to yield 6.624 percent or 47 basis points over the Treasury curve.
J.P. Morgan Securities is lead manager on the deal.
Elsewhere, GTE North issued by competitive bid $250 million A1/AA rated debentures due 2008 at par to yield 6.90 percent or 47 basis points over the 10-year T-note.
Morgan Stanley & Co Inc was the high bidder, it said.
Moving on, WMX Technologies Inc issued $200 million A1/A-plus rated notes due 1998 to yield six percent or 28 basis points over the when-issued two year Treasury.
Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette led the syndicate.
Global issuer Pohang Iron & Steel Co Ltd came to market with $300 million A2/A-plus rated 10-year notes as 7-1/8s to yield 7.141 percent or 70 basis points over Treasuries.
Salomon Brothers was lead manager on the issue.

Outside the primary arena, traders stressed the market was still cash rich and deals were generally well received. Secondary spreads to Treasuries were mostly flat as government prices rallied on a string of bond-friendly economic news.

Treasuries popped higher early after the Labor Department said its employment cost index rose 0.6 percent against forecasts of a 0.8 percent rise, analysts said. Long bond gains doubled after the conference board said its consumer confidence index fell to 106.2 in October from a revised 111.8 in September.

Turning to high-yielders, traders quoted prices marginally higher but the tone continued to suffer from the promise of burgeoning supply through November. Investor caution ahead of myriad economic data also capped gains, traders said.

"The secondary market is quoted better but not necessarily trading better," one head trader said. "The bias here is to sell because employment cost is just one of 800 numbers coming out, plus the election, plus supply."
New high-yield issues were trading firm but so far devoid of the more than one point gains reaped by most deals in recent weeks, dealers said.

National Energy Group's $100 million B1/single-B 10-year 144a senior notes, priced at par late on Monday as 10-3/4s to yield 420 basis points over Treasuries, were quoted at par in aftermarket trading.
The issue was led by a Bear Stearns & Co syndicate.

Traders said they saw no markets yet for the $150 million Australis Holdings 144a B2/CCC-plus rated senior secured discount notes of 2002. The deal was priced early on Tuesday with a four-year zero coupon at 56.07 to yield 15 percent via Salomon Brothers.

Nor was there trading for Unison Healthcare Corp's $100 million 144a B3/single-B rated 10-year senior notes, which were priced by a CIBC Wood Gundy Securities group on Tuesday at par to yield 12.25 percent.
